props.title: Save Money
lines: Building wealth has little to do with your income or investment return, and a lot to do with your savings rate.
You can build wealth without a high return. You cannot build it without a gap between ego and income.

props.title: What the chapter actually argues
items: Past a modest income, your savings rate matters more than your investment rate of return.
Wealth is the gap between your ego and your income. Hide the ego, the gap appears.
Saving is not only for a target purchase. It is flexibility, options, and waiting power.
You do not need a specific reason to save. The reason arrives later, as luck and risk do.
Everyone's savings is a function of their expectations more than their salary.

props.kicker: WHY SAVING BEATS A CLEVER RETURN
props.title: The gap is the strategy

rows.v: Past a modest income, cutting spending 10% can matter more than finding an extra 1% of return.
Wealth is the gap between ego and income. Raise income or lower ego. Both widen the gap.
You do not need a named purchase to justify saving. Flexibility is the purchase.
Savings is how you survive the unplanned: a job loss, a medical bill, a market you want to buy.
Two households with the same salary can have opposite wealth if expectations differ.

props.title: Build the gap on purpose
items: Increase the savings rate before you hunt a fancier strategy.
Hidden lifestyle cuts are more reliable than promised alpha.
Save because your future self will need room, not because a spreadsheet named a yacht.

props.kicker: SAVINGS IS THE M.P.G. OF MONEY
props.title: Control versus hoped-for returns

rows.v: U.S. energy per dollar of G.D.P. is 60% lower than 1950. Average MPG of vehicles on the road has doubled since 1975.
A 1989 Ford Taurus: 18.0 MPG. A 2019 Chevy Suburban: 18.1 MPG. Efficiency moved the world more than geology.
U.S. oil and gas production up 65% since 1975, while conservation more than doubled what we can do with that energy.
Book: if you earn 8% and I earn 12%, but I need half as much to be happy, I can be better off as the worse investor.
Professionals grind for 0.1% of extra return while two or three full points of lifestyle bloat sit unused.

props.note: Chapter 10, as printed. Not a live energy forecast.
